name: markup-color-highlighting-retrieval
description: Evaluate retrieval for research on whether markup, highlighting, color, or formatting can increase instruction salience in multi-turn LLM interaction.

cases.query: LLM multi-turn dialogue HTML markup text highlighting prompt formatting instruction salience
cases.description: Retrieve work studying structured markup, highlighting, visual emphasis, or related mechanisms for making important instructions more salient to language or multimodal models.

judgments.rationale: Directly studies improving instruction following through optimized context construction, but does not test HTML color or visual highlighting.
Separates and identifies instruction spans, including formatting constraints, to improve instruction following, but uses activation steering rather than markup or color.
Optimizes combined textual and visual prompts for multimodal models, providing an adjacent mechanism for visual prompt emphasis, but does not study rendered HTML highlighting in dialogue.
Studies style-controllable multimodal dialogue, but its emphasis is audio-visual dialogue generation rather than highlighting important textual instructions.
Studies structured instructions and noise in long-context processing, but not markup, color, or text highlighting.
Optimizes generated instructions and meta-prompts, but does not investigate formatting-based or visual salience.
Evaluates reasoning over dense multimodal contexts, but does not manipulate visual highlighting or markup to guide attention.
Focuses on detecting LLM-generated Wikipedia text rather than instruction salience or highlighting.
Focuses on graph-based multi-agent routing rather than markup or visual emphasis.
Studies communication complexity in multi-agent reasoning rather than highlighted or visually formatted instructions.
